new_material_candidates.name: Memory as Action: Autonomous Context Curation for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks
new_material_candidates.material_reason: Treats working-memory management itself as a learned policy action, using insertion and deletion operations trained end-to-end with reinforcement learning rather than an external fixed retrieval or summarization policy.

new_material_candidates.name: Learning to Share: Selective Memory for Efficient Parallel Agentic Systems
new_material_candidates.material_reason: Uses a learned reinforcement-trained controller to decide which intermediate steps from parallel agent teams enter a global shared memory, creating a materially distinct selective cross-team memory-admission mechanism.

reference_or_screened.name: CompassMem — Memory Matters More: Event-Centric Memory as a Logic Map for Agent Searching and Reasoning
reference_or_screened.reason: Task 8 previously screened CompassMem as role-adjacent. Its published LoCoMo and NarrativeQA evaluation centers retrieval and reasoning rather than a matched interactive action-selection contract. Current code visibility does not silently change that applicability disposition or establish a cutoff-consistent final revision.

reference_or_screened.name: Selective Memory Retention for Long-Horizon LLM Agents / TraceRetain
reference_or_screened.reason: The work is a workshop paper on bounded retention, not a main-conference ICML baseline identity; no official executable implementation is promoted here, and prior Task-8 role gating remains in force.

reference_or_screened.name: Agent Memory: Characterization and System Implications of Stateful Long-Horizon Workloads
reference_or_screened.reason: The contribution characterizes memory-system behavior and system implications rather than defining one claim-bearing memory method to compare against Hetren.

reference_or_screened.name: Mem2ActBench
reference_or_screened.reason: Mem2ActBench tests whether memory supports tool selection and parameter grounding; it is useful for applicability analysis but is not itself a competing memory policy.

reference_or_screened.name: M-star — Every Task Deserves Its Own Memory Harness
reference_or_screened.reason: M-star evolves task-specific executable memory programs using benchmark feedback. Its meta-optimization and evaluation-information contract is materially different from a directly matched frozen runtime memory comparator and requires a separate information-opportunity and tuning-parity analysis.
